narrative:
The model determined that you have a 43% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability is high enough to cross the bank's threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly shaped this outcome were the length of the loan you requested, your credit history, and your employment situation. The requested duration of 48 months was the single biggest reason for the rejection. Most approved applicants ask for loans around 19 months, so your four-year term pushed the prediction noticeably toward bad credit risk. Your past delays in repaying credit also worked against you; while most approved customers have a clean record of existing paid credits, your history of late payments increased the model's concern. Finally, being unemployed pulled the prediction in the same negative direction. Only about 7% of approved applicants are unemployed, whereas most have been steadily employed for several years.

Taken together, these three pieces of information led the model to conclude that the risk was too high to approve the loan.

What you should do next is focus on the areas you can change. Try to build a stronger credit history by making all payments on time, look for stable employment, and when you reapply, request a shorter loan period. These steps will improve your profile and raise your chances of approval in the future. (218 words)
